name: Ethical AI
description: The role of AI, AGI, ASI and QI in humanity and society, and how organisations determine and define their position.
accountabilities: Set the organisation's position on AI's role in society, and keep it current as capability advances towards AGI and beyond.
Decide where AI should and should not be used, and the human oversight it requires.
Give the board a clear view of the ethical questions AI raises for the organisation.
keyQuestion: What is our position on AI, and would we be comfortable defending it publicly?

name: Governance
description: Responsible AI, risk, assurance, accountability, regulation and board oversight.
accountabilities: Establish AI risk, assurance and accountability frameworks.
Align AI use with regulation and emerging standards.
Give the board clear oversight of AI use, performance and incidents.
keyQuestion: Who is accountable when an AI system gets it wrong?

name: Strategy
description: Enterprise AI strategy, portfolio choices, investment and alignment.
accountabilities: Set the enterprise AI strategy and investment portfolio.
Align AI priorities with the organisation's strategy.
Decide where to build, buy or partner.
keyQuestion: Where will AI create the most advantage for us over the next three years?

name: Transformation
description: Operating-model and process transformation enabled by AI.
accountabilities: Redesign operating models and processes around AI.
Sequence change across functions and business units.
Manage the dependencies between technology, people and process.
keyQuestion: Which parts of how we work should be redesigned, not just automated?

name: Value
description: Business cases, benefits, productivity, growth and value realisation.
accountabilities: Build credible business cases for AI investment.
Track benefits, productivity and growth against those cases.
Scale or stop initiatives on the evidence.
keyQuestion: How do we know our AI investment is paying off?

name: Capability
description: Data, platforms, models, agents, architecture, vendors and organisational capability.
accountabilities: Ensure the data, platforms and architecture AI depends on.
Make sound model, agent and vendor choices.
Build the organisation's AI skills and teams.
keyQuestion: Do we have the data, platforms and people to deliver our AI ambitions?

name: Adoption
description: Workforce, skills, change, behaviours and organisational adoption.
accountabilities: Lead workforce skills and change.
Shape the behaviours and ways of working AI requires.
Measure uptake and sustained, safe use.
keyQuestion: Are our people using AI well, and safely?

name: Operating AI
description: The continual management, improvement and optimisation of the operation of AI models, agents and systems, workflows, and outputs.
accountabilities: Monitor the performance of models, agents and workflows in operation.
Continually improve and optimise their outputs.
Manage cost, reliability and change over time.
keyQuestion: Are our AI systems still performing as intended, and getting better?
